{{Short description|American geographer and landscape ecologist (born 1959)}}
{{for|the English swimmer|Janet Franklin (swimmer)}}
'''Janet Franklin''' (born July 8, 1959 in [[Frankfurt]], Germany<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/janet-franklin-8o7ila/|title=Janet Franklin|website=www.nasonline.org|publisher=National Academy of Sciences|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190324141218/http://www.nasonline.org/member-directory/members/20033171.html|archive-date=2019-03-24|url-status=live|access-date=2019-02-03}}</ref>) is an American [[geographer]], [[Botany|botanist]], and [[Landscape ecology|landscape ecologist]]. Her work is centered on the use of [[remote sensing]] to model and understand vegetated landscapes. She is currently a Distinguished Professor of [[Biogeography]] in the Department of Botany and Plant Sciences at the [[University of California, Riverside]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://plantbiology.ucr.edu/people/faculty/franklin.html|title=Department of Botany & Plant Sciences: Faculty|website=plantbiology.ucr.edu|access-date=2019-02-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190204014602/https://plantbiology.ucr.edu/people/faculty/franklin.html|archive-date=2019-02-04|url-status=live}}</ref>
== Early life and education ==
Franklin grew up near San Francisco.<ref name=":0" /> She received a [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] in Environmental Biology from the [[University of California, Santa Barbara|University of California Santa Barbara]] in 1979. Subsequently, she received a [[Master of Arts|master's degree]] from UCSB in Geography in 1983, and finally a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] from the same institution in 1988.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=https://sustainability.asu.edu/person/|title=Janet Franklin - Person|website=Julie Ann Wrigley Global Institute of Sustainability|language=en-US|access-date=2019-02-03}}</ref> Her thesis focused on the remote sensing of woody vegetation structures in Mali.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://geog.ucsb.edu/ucsb-geography-in-the-1980s-a-mini-memoir-from-janet-franklin/|title=UCSB Geography in the 1980s: A Mini-Memoir from Janet Franklin - UC Geography|website=geog.ucsb.edu|access-date=2019-02-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190204014512/https://geog.ucsb.edu/ucsb-geography-in-the-1980s-a-mini-memoir-from-janet-franklin/|archive-date=2019-02-04|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sites.google.com/a/asu.edu/vale-lab/janet-franklin-page|title=Janet Franklin - VALE Lab|website=sites.google.com|access-date=2019-02-03|archive-date=2020-05-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200526133935/https://sites.google.com/a/asu.edu/vale-lab/janet-franklin-page|url-status=dead}}</ref> 

==Career==
Franklin received her start in remote sensing as a doctoral candidate when she was recruited by a professor on the basis of her ability to distinguish different species of pine tree from aerial photographs.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|last=Giles|first=Nathan|date=2016-02-22|title=Janet Franklin adds complexity to the climate change map|url=https://www.aaas.org/janet-franklin-adds-complexity-climate-change-map|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190204014827/https://www.aaas.org/janet-franklin-adds-complexity-climate-change-map|archive-date=2019-02-04|access-date=2019-02-03|website=American Association for the Advancement of Science|language=en}}</ref>

In 1988, Franklin began teaching and researching at [[San Diego State University]], where she remained until 2009. Her 1995 paper, ''Predictive vegetation mapping: geographic modeling of biospatial patterns in relation to environmental gradients'', is considered a foundational work of modern, remote sensing-based landscape ecology. In 2009, she was appointed as a professor of geography at [[Arizona State University]], becoming a Regent's Professor in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sols.asu.edu/janet-franklin|title=Janet Franklin {{!}} School of Life Sciences|website=sols.asu.edu|language=en|access-date=2019-02-03|archive-date=2019-04-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190424041533/https://sols.asu.edu/janet-franklin|url-status=dead}}</ref> From 2014 to 2016, she was president of the US chapter of the International Association of Landscape Ecology.<ref name=":0" /> Some of her research has focused on island ecosystems in the West Indies and Polynesia. In 2017, she was appointed to the University of California Riverside.<ref name=":1" />

Franklin's work focuses on the use of remote sensing techniques to model and understand vegetated landscapes.<ref name=":2" /> She has made significant contributions to the study of human-caused landscape change and predictive vegetation mapping.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Alumna Janet Franklin Honored for Ecosystems Work {{!}} UC Geography|url=https://geog.ucsb.edu/alumna-janet-franklin-honored-for-ecosystems-work/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190204014652/https://geog.ucsb.edu/alumna-janet-franklin-honored-for-ecosystems-work/|archive-date=2019-02-04|access-date=2019-02-03|website=geog.ucsb.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Staff|first=A. A. G.|date=2015-05-18|title=Janet Franklin inducted into National Academy of Science; joins the other NAS members at Arizona State University|url=http://news.aag.org/2015/05/janet-franklin-inducted-into-nas/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190204014427/http://news.aag.org/2015/05/janet-franklin-inducted-into-nas/|archive-date=2019-02-04|access-date=2019-02-03|website=AAG Newsletter|language=en-US}}</ref> In recent years, much of her work has focused on climate change, both [[Climate change|present]] and [[Climate change (general concept)|historical]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Sheriff|first=Natasja|date=2015-11-12|title=What The Last Ice Age Tells Us About Protecting Birds from Climate Change Now|url=https://www.audubon.org/news/what-last-ice-age-tells-us-about-protecting-birds-climate-change-now|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190204065838/https://www.audubon.org/news/what-last-ice-age-tells-us-about-protecting-birds-climate-change-now|archive-date=2019-02-04|access-date=2019-02-03|website=Audubon|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Hays|first=Brooks|date=2017-07-29|title=Climate change pushed songbirds from Bahamas in the wake of the last ice age|url=https://www.upi.com/Climate-change-pushed-songbirds-from-Bahamas-in-the-wake-of-the-last-ice-age/9651504014802/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190204014328/https://www.upi.com/Climate-change-pushed-songbirds-from-Bahamas-in-the-wake-of-the-last-ice-age/9651504014802/|archive-date=2019-02-04|access-date=2019-02-03|website=UPI|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Mastroianni|first=Brian|date=2015-11-23|title=Which is worse for wildlife - climate change or humans?|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/humans-contributed-more-species-loss-than-climate-change/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190204014559/https://www.cbsnews.com/news/humans-contributed-more-species-loss-than-climate-change/|archive-date=2019-02-04|access-date=2019-02-03|website=www.cbsnews.com|language=en-US}}</ref>

Franklin is a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]]<ref name=":0" /> and a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]], the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] and the [[Ecological Society of America]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-05-07 |title=Ecological Society of America announces 2015 Fellows |url=https://esa.org/blog/2015/05/07/ecological-society-of-america-announces-2015-fellows/ |access-date=2025-08-12 |website=Ecological Society of America}}</ref> She is also the current editor-in-chief of ''[[Diversity and Distributions|Diversity & Distributions]],'' a highly ranked journal on conservation biogeography.

== Selected works ==
Franklin is the author of one book and over 120 peer-reviewed academic papers.<ref name=":3" />

=== Book ===
* Franklin, Janet. ''Mapping species distributions: spatial inference and prediction''. Cambridge University Press, 2010.

=== Articles ===
* Franklin, Janet. "Predictive vegetation mapping: geographic modelling of biospatial patterns in relation to environmental gradients." ''Progress in physical geography'' 19, no. 4 (1995)
* Franklin, Janet. "Predicting the distribution of shrub species in southern California from climate and terrain‐derived variables." ''Journal of Vegetation Science'' 9, no. 5 (1998)
* Franklin, Janet. "Moving beyond static species distribution models in support of conservation biogeography." ''Diversity and Distributions'' 16, no. 3 (2010)
* Franklin, Janet, et al. "Modeling plant species distributions under future climates: how fine scale do climate projections need to be?." ''Global change biology'' 19.2 (2013)
